links.targetTitle: The PSM is priced as a zero-capital-requirement route to ASC

title: Base Rate adjustment is deliberately left discretionary: the numeric guidance is explicitly non-binding
content:
A.3.1.1.1.1 says the Core Executor Agents "should modify the Base Rate on a daily basis, as necessary, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor," and A.3.1.1.1.1.1 labels its PSM-ASC step table as "non-binding guidelines." The word choice throughout is *should consider*, never *must set*.

This is a real design choice rather than vagueness. A binding table would make rate-setting mechanical and predictable — and therefore front-runnable, and blind to conditions the table does not encode. The Atlas instead publishes the reaction function as a prior so the market can anticipate behaviour, while reserving discretion for cases where following it would be wrong.

The discretion is bounded on three sides. First, mandated inputs: the external interest-rate environment including competitors' rates and both DeFi and TradFi funding rates (A.3.1.1.1.1.2), plus "long-term market stability, user stability, system sustainability, and growth" (A.3.1.1.1.1.3). Second, a required counterparty — the Core Council Risk Advisor. Third, a hard technical ceiling on how far and how fast the rate can move, imposed by the bounded external access module.

A.3.1.1.1.1.3 adds a constraint that cuts against daily adjustment: agents must consider "constraints on Primes, including their cost of capital and reaction time, to avoid creating unnecessary volatility in rates." The permission to move daily is thus paired with an instruction not to, absent reason — the counterparties who must re-price against the Base Rate cannot absorb arbitrary churn.

A.3.1.1.1.1.2.1 turns one input into an obligation: agents "must develop automated tools to monitor the external interest-rate environment." Discretion is expected to become better-informed over time, not to be replaced.
description: Agents may move the rate daily in consultation with a Risk Advisor, weighing external rates, sustainability and growth — so the PSM-ASC table is a prior, not a control algorithm.
